style_when: the story is a product, a device, a price or a market for a thing the reader could buy — an appliance, a panel, a router, a robot arm
prompt: Studio product photograph inside a residential garage: a low rounded robot lawn mower with a deep pine green hull, burnt-orange trim and knobby rear wheels, parked at a three-quarter angle on the left third of a sealed concrete floor. Staged low on the right, a boxed replacement battery kit beside an opened six-pack of thin steel pivot blades on a folded cloth. Single softbox key light from the upper left, visible falloff, long contact shadows raking across the dusty concrete; deep pine green, graphite and ochre against off-white drywall falling into shadow. 50mm lens, shallow depth of field, subtle film grain. Extreme asymmetry, generous negative space, no people, no text, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, numbers, watermarks, logos
rationale: The story turns on a purchasable appliance and the recurring bill its spec pages hide, so a catalogue-clear product shot in a real garage makes the economics visible: the machine beside the battery kit and blade pack that quietly add a quarter to its price. Studio_object gives the hero tactile weight, directional light and a long contact shadow instead of a sterile sweep, and it rotates the desk away from the recent still-life, telephoto and collage treatments.
subject: an unbranded robot lawn mower with a boxed replacement battery kit and an opened blade six-pack staged beside it on a garage floor
core_thesis: Husqvarna's own spec pages quietly price a robot mower's life support — $26.99 blade packs on a 3-4 month clock and a $313.36 battery inside a 2-5 year band — so a $2,599.99 machine bills roughly a quarter more over four years.
core_conflict: The one-time purchase price and payback division that sells the machine versus the maker's printed wear schedule — blade and battery clocks — that keeps billing after the sale.
composition: Extreme asymmetry: the mower commands the left third at a three-quarter angle, the battery kit and blade six-pack staged low on the right, generous empty floor and wall above for editorial breathing room
alt_text: Robot lawn mower in a garage with a boxed replacement battery and blade six-pack staged on the concrete beside it
caption: The spec pages price the mower's life support at $26.99 a blade pack and $313.36 a battery — about a quarter of the machine again.
title: Robot mower with its hidden blade and battery bill
